svg.title: The key part on the high-level design: the queue and the message store
svg.desc: The whole design with the queue (Kafka) and the message store (Cassandra) in focus. Key part: accept 100k messages a second and never lose an accepted message. Messages get 100k writes and 10k status reads a second by message_id, are kept 30 days, and are spread across nodes by message_id. The queue is a log on disk with 3 copies that replays after a crash, so Kafka; RabbitMQ would win if per-message delays mattered more than volume. The message store spreads writes by message_id, so Cassandra; PostgreSQL would win if the data fit one node.

text.tspan: Key part: accept 100k/s, never lose an accepted message
Messages: 100k writes/s, 10k status reads/s by message_id; kept 30 days
Queue: log on disk with 3 copies, replay after a crash -> Kafka
alt: RabbitMQ, if per-message delays mattered more than volume
Message store: writes spread by message_id -> Cassandra
alt: PostgreSQL, if the data fit one node
